strengths: Well-motivated autoregressive approach with clear advantages for scene completion and outpainting tasks; naturally supports incremental construction paradigm
Strong quantitative results on shape synthesis (SOTA on PhotoShape: FID 5.68 vs L3DG 8.49) with cleaner Gaussian allocations
Thoughtfully designed technical components: separate position/feature vocabularies, 3D RoPE for spatial awareness, LFQ for better codebook utilization
Comprehensive experimental coverage: ablations on serialization strategies, real-world validation on ScanNet++, extensive implementation details and reproducibility information
Excellent presentation: clear methodology, detailed configurations, thorough appendix, well-organized writing
Flexible inference capabilities naturally supported: temperature-based sampling, tree search for connectivity, masking for constraints
weaknesses: Scene generation results lack quantitative evaluation; comparison to L3DG and other baselines is primarily visual/qualitative, making it impossible to assess whether scenes are actually superior to diffusion methods
Significant degradation on real-world data (ScanNet++): visible artifacts, noisy geometry, acknowledged autoencoder reconstruction fidelity bottleneck limits practical applicability
Slow inference for large scenes (~1.67 hours for 12m×12m on GH200 GPU); requires multiple resampling attempts; no timing comparison to diffusion or other baselines provided
Limited baseline comparisons for scene generation: only L3DG compared; no comparisons to DiffuScene, SceneFormer, or other recent scene generation methods
Claimed advantages over diffusion (compositionality, diversity, single-pass generation) not quantitatively validated; iterative outpainting partially undermines single-pass claim
Sequence ordering ablation lacks depth: explanation relies on '3D RoPE compensates' without theoretical justification; no analysis of what patterns different orderings capture
Scope limited to structured indoor scenes with regular layouts; generalization to outdoor/unstructured environments unclear; real-world domain gap is substantial
Missing quantitative metrics for scenes: no FID/KID, diversity measures, or scene-specific quality metrics; unclear if this is engineering limitation or fundamental disadvantage
Chunking introduces design choices (overlap strategy, window positioning) requiring careful tuning; boundary effects across chunks not systematically analyzed
Insufficient ablations: no study of chunk size effects, transformer architecture choices, vocabulary size sensitivity, or failure mode analysis
